nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-02.title: Quadratic in √x
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-02.body:
Let $t=\sqrt x\ge0$. Then $2t^2+t-1=0$, $(2t-1)(t+1)=0$. Since $t\ge0$, $t=\frac12$ and $x=\frac14$. Check: $\frac12+\frac12-1=0$. ✓

**Answer: $x=\frac14$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-02.title: Isolate the root
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-02.body:
$\sqrt x=1-2x$ requires $x\le\frac12$. Squaring, $x=1-4x+4x^2$, so $4x^2-5x+1=0$, $(4x-1)(x-1)=0$. Only $x=\frac14$ satisfies $x\le\frac12$.

**Answer: $x=\frac14$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-03.title: Count by first digit
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-03.body:
With at most four digits, a number above $4000$ must use all four digits and start with $5$ or $7$. The remaining three digits can be arranged in $3!=6$ ways, giving $2\cdot6=12$.

**Answer: $12$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-04.title: Right trapezoid
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-04.body:
The centers are $3+12=15$ apart. The radii to the two tangent points are perpendicular to the line, forming a right trapezoid with parallel sides $3$ and $12$. Dropping a perpendicular from the smaller center gives a right triangle with hypotenuse $15$ and leg $12-3=9$, so the tangent segment is $\sqrt{15^2-9^2}=12$.

**Answer: $12$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-04.title: Formula
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-04.body:
For externally tangent circles with radii $r,R$, the common external tangent has length $\sqrt{(r+R)^2-(R-r)^2}=2\sqrt{rR}=2\sqrt{36}=12$.

**Answer: $12$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-05.title: Count pairs
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-05.body:
The sum is odd exactly when one number is odd and one is even: $10\cdot10=100$ pairs, out of $\binom{20}{2}=190$. Probability $\frac{100}{190}=\frac{10}{19}$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{19}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-05.title: Condition on the first pick
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-05.body:
Whatever the first number, $10$ of the remaining $19$ numbers have the opposite parity, so the probability is $\frac{10}{19}$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}{19}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-06.title: Split by the longest side
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-06.body:
Let the third side be $x$; the triangle inequality gives $4\le x\le20$.
- If $x$ is the longest side, the triangle is obtuse when $x^2>81+144=225$, i.e. $x\ge16$: $x=16,\dots,20$ ($5$ values).
- If $12$ is the longest side, it is obtuse when $144>81+x^2$, i.e. $x^2<63$: $x=4,5,6,7$ ($4$ values).

Total $9$.

**Answer: $9$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-08.title: AM is a diameter
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-08.body:
The radius at $M$ is perpendicular to $BC$, and so is the altitude $AM$. Hence the center lies on $AM$, and since $A$ is on the circle, $AM$ is a diameter. Then $\angle ADM=90^\circ$, so $MD\perp AC$. In right triangle $MDC$, $MC=6$ and $\angle C=60^\circ$, so $DC=6\cos60^\circ=3$.

**Answer: $3$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-08.title: Power of a point
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-08.body:
$C$ is outside the circle; its tangent length is $CM=6$ and line $CA$ meets the circle at $D$ and $A$. So $CD\cdot CA=CM^2$, i.e. $CD\cdot12=36$, $CD=3$.

**Answer: $3$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-09.title: Glue them together
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-09.body:
Treat David and Jan as one block: $3!$ orders of the block and the other two, times $2$ orders inside the block, gives $12$ of the $4!=24$ arrangements. Probability $\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-09.title: Adjacent positions
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-09.body:
David and Jan occupy a random pair of the $\binom42=6$ position pairs; $3$ pairs are adjacent. Probability $\frac36=\frac12$.

**Answer: $\frac12$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-10.title: Group by denominator
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-10.body:
For denominator $d$ the fractions $\frac1d,\dots,\frac{d-1}{d}$ sum to $\frac{(d-1)d/2}{d}=\frac{d-1}{2}$. Summing over $d=2,\dots,50$:
$$\frac12(1+2+\dots+49)=\frac12\cdot1225=\frac{1225}{2}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{1225}{2}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-10.title: Pair complementary fractions
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-10.body:
For each denominator $d$, pair $\frac kd$ with $\frac{d-k}{d}$; each pair sums to $1$, so the $d-1$ fractions average $\frac12$. There are $1+2+\dots+49=1225$ fractions in all, so the sum is $\frac{1225}{2}$.

**Answer: $\frac{1225}{2}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-11.title: Area two ways
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-11.body:
$5^2+12^2=13^2$, so it is a right triangle with area $\frac12\cdot5\cdot12=30$. The shortest altitude is to the longest side: $h=\frac{2\cdot30}{13}=\frac{60}{13}$ (the other altitudes are $12$ and $5$).

**Answer: $\frac{60}{13}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-12.title: Shift and subtract
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-12.body:
Let $S$ be the sum. Then $\frac S7=\frac1{7^2}+\frac2{7^3}+\dots$, and
$$S-\frac S7=\frac17+\frac1{7^2}+\frac1{7^3}+\dots=\frac{1/7}{1-1/7}=\frac16.$$
So $\frac67S=\frac16$ and $S=\frac{7}{36}$.

**Answer: $\frac{7}{36}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-13.title: Inclusion–exclusion
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-13.body:
Students taking at least one: $17+19-11=25$. Neither: $32-25=7$.

**Answer: $7$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-14.title: Discriminant zero
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-14.body:
Setting $2x^2=-4x+k$: $2x^2+4x-k=0$ has exactly one root when $16+8k=0$, so $k=-2$.

**Answer: $-2$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-14.title: Tangent slope
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-14.body:
The line has slope $-4$; the parabola's slope $4x=-4$ at $x=-1$, where $y=2$. The tangent line there is $y=-4x-2$, so $k=-2$.

**Answer: $-2$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-15.title: Prime factorization
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-15.body:
$12250=2\cdot5^3\cdot7^2$. To make every exponent even, multiply by $2\cdot5=10$: $122500=350^2$.

**Answer: $10$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-16.title: Diagonals
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-16.body:
Let the diagonals be $d$ and $2d$. Then $A=\frac12\cdot d\cdot2d=d^2$, so $d=\sqrt A$. The diagonals bisect each other at right angles, so a side is $\sqrt{\left(\frac d2\right)^2+d^2}=\frac{\sqrt5}{2}d$. The perimeter is $4\cdot\frac{\sqrt5}{2}\sqrt A=2\sqrt{5A}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{5A}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-17.title: Set x = 1
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-17.body:
The sum of the coefficients of a polynomial $P(x)$ is $P(1)=(3-1)^7=2^7=128$.

**Answer: $128$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-18.title: R = abc/(4K)
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-18.body:
The altitude to the base $10$ is $\sqrt{12^2-5^2}=\sqrt{119}$, so the area is $K=5\sqrt{119}$. Then
$$R=\frac{abc}{4K}=\frac{10\cdot12\cdot12}{20\sqrt{119}}=\frac{72}{\sqrt{119}}=\frac{72\sqrt{119}}{119}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{72\sqrt{119}}{119}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-18.title: Center on the altitude
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-18.body:
The center lies on the altitude from the apex, at distance $R$ from the apex and from a base vertex. With the base vertex $5$ units from the foot of the altitude: $(\sqrt{119}-R)^2+25=R^2$, so $144=2\sqrt{119}R$ and $R=\frac{72}{\sqrt{119}}=\frac{72\sqrt{119}}{119}$.

**Answer: $\frac{72\sqrt{119}}{119}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-19.title: Half-chord
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-19.body:
The perpendicular from the center bisects the chord. Half the chord is $\sqrt{8^2-5^2}=\sqrt{39}$, so the chord is $2\sqrt{39}$.

**Answer: $2\sqrt{39}$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-21.title: Multiply the areas
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-21.body:
If the edges are $a,b,c$ with $ab=20$, $bc=25$, $ca=80$, then $(abc)^2=20\cdot25\cdot80=40000$, so $V=abc=200$.

**Answer: $200$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-22.title: Apothem 12
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-22.body:
The circle's radius is the hexagon's apothem, the height of each of the six equilateral triangles. A side is $\frac{2\cdot12}{\sqrt3}=8\sqrt3$. Area $=\frac12\cdot\text{perimeter}\cdot\text{apothem}=\frac12\cdot48\sqrt3\cdot12=288\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $288\sqrt3$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-24.title: Relative speed
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-24.body:
The minute hand moves $6^\circ$ per minute and the hour hand $0.5^\circ$ per minute, so the angle between them grows at $5.5^\circ$ per minute. They are first perpendicular after $\frac{90}{5.5}=\frac{180}{11}=16\frac{4}{11}$ minutes. $\frac4{11}$ min $=\frac{240}{11}\approx21.8$ s, so the time is about 12:16:22.

**Answer: 12:16:22**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-25.title: Add rates
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-25.body:
Together they paint $\frac18+\frac16=\frac{7}{24}$ of the room per hour, so they need $\frac{24}{7}$ hours.

**Answer: $\frac{24}{7}$ hours**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-26.title: Factor
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-26.body:
$(x-y)(x+y)=45$ with $0<x-y<x+y$ of the same parity (both odd here). The factor pairs are $1\cdot45$, $3\cdot15$, $5\cdot9$, giving $(x,y)=(23,22),(9,6),(7,2)$.

**Answer: $(7,2),(9,6),(23,22)$**

nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-29.title: Cycle of units digits
nyciml-1999-00-fall-seniorb-29.body:
The units digit of $37^n$ follows that of $7^n$: $7,9,3,1$ repeating with period $4$. Since $73\equiv1\pmod4$, the units digit is $7$.

**Answer: $7$**
